answer: The pewterer strikes his touch mark into every piece and books the alloy and the date. A echo piece struck in another shop fails the register: at the mesa of the mark the punch must match the pewterer's own die, and a home-struck mark is shallow and crooked. Forging a touch mark means bribing a pewterer, faking a year of entries and paying 16,200, and the tundra record in the guild book is kept for life, so a piece whose mark was never entered is melted down.
